newsitem.title: UK: Princess Diana in love with Moslem doctor - paper.
newsitem.headline: Princess Diana in love with Moslem doctor - paper.

text.p: Britain's Princess Diana has fallen in love with a 36-year-old Moslem heart surgeon and wants him to become her second husband after heir to the throne Prince Charles, a British newspaper claimed on Sunday.

In a story splashed over most of its first five pages, the Sunday Mirror linked the divorced Princess's name to Hasnat Khan, an unmarried British-based cardiac specialist whose family lives in Pakistan.
And it quoted a "friend" of the 36-year-old Princess as saying she hoped he would father a half-sister to her two sons, Princes William and Harry.
"The Princess is desperately in love," the tabloid quoted an unnamed "friend" of Diana as saying.
"On the one hand, she wants the world to know. But on the other hand, she is understandably concerned that her enthusiasm may send him running."
The newspaper said the Princess met Khan just over a year ago -- well before her divorce from Charles was finalised.
It said he was one of a team of surgeons who carried out a triple heart bypass operation at London's Royal Brompton Hospital on the husband of her acupuncturist, 70-year-old Joseph Toffolo.

The newspaper said her affections for Khan explained a number of previously surprising developments in the Princess's life -- her regular night-time visits to the Royal Brompton to comfort patients, and trips to Pakistan and Australia.
Diana paid a two-day visit to Lahore, Pakistan in February to visit a cancer hospital sponsored by the country's former international cricket captain Imran Khan, no relation to Hasnat.
The paper said it was now "widely believed" she took the chance to visit Hasnat Khan's family, who had approved a possible marriage even though the Princess would not convert to Islam.
Diana is currently visiting Sydney, Australia to lend her support to an institute involved in the fight against heart disease.
The Sunday Mirror said Hasnat had worked under Victor Chang, after whom the institute is named, during his early career.
One of the unnamed "friends" on which the paper relied for its story was quoted as saying the Princess would like a daughter to complete her family.
"She's made it clear that she wants to add to her family," the friend said.
